core.title: Declare only an in-family runtime in a test's runtime header
core.given: A test file collected and executed by the stack's test suite
core.when: its header declares the optional runtime field (any existing or new declaration, regardless of what was edited)
core.then: The declared runtime MUST be one of the stack's test runtime family — the runtimes the suite's runner can actually execute under (profile-supplied vocabulary).
prefer: Declare the runtime the suite actually executes under.
Or drop the runtime declaration entirely; the suite's runner is already known.
If the test genuinely belongs to a runtime outside the family, move it to the suite of that runtime instead of relabelling it.
avoid: Declaring a runtime outside the family on a test the suite collects — it is mislabelled or filed in the wrong suite.

Restricting test runtime declarations to the source-side runtime vocabulary the profile supplies (idiom.source_syntax#source_runtime_values); the test vocabulary is deliberately the wider execution family of the runner.
unless: The test has no runtime declaration — the field is optional for tests and absence is not flagged.
core.why: Every test file in this stack is collected and executed by the suite's runner, a runtime in that family, whatever its header claims; a declaration outside the family makes the gate attribute the test to a runner that never executed it.
evidence: The stack's test-discipline check reports no runtime-family finding for any test file collected by the suite.
Every collected test file either lacks a runtime declaration or its declared value is in the profile's test runtime family.
verification: Judge only test files that declare a runtime: parse the test header for the runtime declaration (syntax from the profile) and skip files without the field — for a test the field is optional and the runner is already known.

The allowed vocabulary is the profile's test runtime family: the runtimes the test runner can actually execute under. The test-side vocabulary is deliberately wider than the profile's source-side runtime vocabulary (idiom.source_syntax#source_runtime_values); do not apply the source-side list to test headers.
Test membership is decided by what the suite collects, not by a path glob, and the check judges the current file state including unchanged existing headers — no edit-history condition.
Term declared_runtime: the optional runtime declaration on a test (syntax from the profile).
Per-rule enforcement: severity 2, disposition strict — fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: test file collected and executed by the stack's test suite
test file whose header declares the optional runtime field
runtime-family finding reported by the stack's test-discipline check on a test file

fires: A test file collected by the suite declares a runtime from outside the family, whether or not that file or header was touched in the current change.
Any collected test declares a runtime value outside the profile's test runtime family.
The stack's test-discipline check reports a runtime-family finding on a test file.
doesNotFire: A test file with no runtime declaration at all (the field is optional for tests).
A test declaring any value in the test runtime family, even though non-test source files are limited to the narrower source-side vocabulary.
A non-test source file's runtime declaration (governed by source-side routing rules, not this one).

profileRequirements.meaning: The runner that collects and executes the test files; its collection defines test membership (no path glob), and it anchors the family the declaration is checked against.
The header construct by which a test file declares its runtime; optional on tests, and files without it are skipped.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `// Runtime: <value>` (optional line-comment header field on test files)

profileRequirements.meaning: The runtime values a test header may declare: the execution family of the stack's test runner, deliberately wider than the source-side runtime vocabulary.
profileRequirements.bunValue: bun, browser, isomorphic, typescript, ts, node, js, javascript, deno, vite, astro, preact

profileRequirements.meaning: The runtime vocabulary allowed on non-test source files' runtime declarations; the test-side family is deliberately wider than this list, and this check must not apply it to test headers.

neutralityNotes: The family boundary is inherently toolchain data (which runtimes the test runner can execute), so the enumerated vocabularies are carried by the profile (vocabulary v3 map entries: tooling.test_harness#test_runtime_family for the test-side family, idiom.source_syntax#source_runtime_values for the narrower source-side list, idiom.source_syntax#runtime_declaration for the header syntax). Detector, shared-policy-node and finding ids are realization details kept in bunOnly; per-rule severity 2 and strict disposition stay in core:verification per policy. Concrete examples (`// Runtime: bun`, `python`, the in-family value lists in fires/doesNotFire) are not repeated in the core because bun.json is delivered as the worked reference example.
